A model-based reinforcement learning approach is investigated for a single agent learning task, using a graph graphed transition model (GBTM) that maps multiple tasks to a unified natural number, based on shared elements between tasks. This allows the agent to avoid redundant exploration and learning, by utilizing previously acquired knowledge when encountering similar states in new tasks. The agent's efficiency in exploration and learning processes is enhanced, by leveraging the shared components of the GBTM through a modular structure, implemented via an attention-based dynamic modular system (AMDMS). The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated in various reinforcement learning tasks, including locomotion and object manipulation tasks with a real robotic arm, and the results indicate the agent's ability to efficiently explore and learn new tasks, by utilizing the shared elements of the GBTM.

The article provides a method to derive a specific identity related to a given function $u$ that satisfies a modified version of the porous medium equation or a related time-dependent equation on a complete, non-compact metric measure space. To achieve this, the authors have devised an approximation scheme to create a sequence of compact approximation domains. This sequence approximates the original infinite volume domain while maintaining the essential properties of the original problem. Through this approach, the authors can prove the desired identity for the modified equations under a less restrictive condition on the underlying space than previously established results. Notably, the authors' methodology is applicable to a broader class of equations and settings, including cases where the underlying space does not have a specific curvature bound. Moreover, the authors' approach may contribute to the development of approximation theory for solutions to nonlinear parabolic equations.

We present a striking and minimal proof of the undecidability of Godel's second incompleteness statement within a specific-predicate axiomatic theory of decidability. Furthermore, it can be regarded as a variant of Godel's second incompleteness theorem. Under the standard assumption that "1 is a prime number" is unprovable within this theory, the theory's undecidability follows from the unprovability of Godel's number in it. This assumption is equivalent to the unprovability of consistency. Thus, we can derive the undecidability of any system capable of proving Godel's number and consistency, including Rosser's strengthened theory.

In three-dimensional space, a function $f$ belonging to the space of regular functions with respect to a Clifford operator is expressed as a sum of a scalar part and a directed part, consisting of the product of the position vector and a regular scalar part. Functions with only a directed part are referred to as monogenic functions. This paper establishes an eigenfunction theory for the Laplacian on a three-dimensional sphere, proving that monogenic eigenfunctions can be represented by a closed differential form using a specific operator, and characterizing regular functions within a region bounded by three concentric spheres in terms of the values of functions and their normal derivatives on the surfaces of that region. This representation formula is analogous to the Hadamard formula in complex analysis and can be reduced to the classical Dirichlet formula when the eigenvalue is positive.

This paper introduces an innovative balanced sampling technique that sequentially selects a geographically balanced representative group from various populations spread across different regions.

By incorporating the idea of balanced selection into time series data and showing its applicability to multiple case studies, including gradual population growth and widespread disease testing scenarios. Our method can be fine-tuned to adjust to changing variables over time and provides a efficient computational solution using the simulated annealing algorithm.

Robots that utilize eye-in-hand cameras are affected by lens distortion and perspective when identifying objects, which can be mitigated by adjusting the camera's parameters. Calibrating the camera using only images of objects perceived by the robot is often made difficult due to the requirement for square, front-facing target images. In this research, we allow for the use of perspective-induced deviations and adjust the parameters based on a single, arbitrarily captured image. The proposed method involves a human presenting the robot with an object and adjusting the object's pose until the detected positions of the object's corners by the camera match their actual positions. This adjustment process is essentially a four-degree of freedom problem, solvable from any captured image. The method was validated through experiments with a JACO 2 manipulator and the AIS350K dataset, demonstrating successful adjustment of the camera parameters in end-effort controlled scenarios. A python implementation is provided for the method.

In solving inverse problems, especially when using Bayesian methods, one often encounters the problem of generating high-probability solutions and sampling the entire posterior distribution. This is a computationally demanding task, particularly with large datasets, as traditional methods such as importance sampling and neural network-based approaches struggle to efficiently model the data distribution due to the heavy tails in the posterior. To address this, we propose a novel regularized conditional generative adversarial network approach that can efficiently sample the posterior, even in situations where the data dimensionality is significantly higher than can be practically managed. Our method is tested on the tomographic image reconstruction problem and demonstrates improved performance in capturing the full posterior distribution, including low-probability regions, compared to other approaches.

We examine linear fractional dynamical systems of the type $\frac{dx}{dt} = Ax$, where $A$ is a constant matrix, and investigate conditions under which invariant surfaces exist. We demonstrate that invariant planes exist if and only if the matrix $A$ contains a specific submatrix structure, and further, that these invariant planes are uniquely determined by the time derivative of $A$. Additionally, we explore the complexity of solving higher-order dynamical systems using a benchmark model, and find that solutions to these models can only be expressed in integer time for a limited set of initial conditions.

Next-generation wireless networks must overcome extremely short wireless signal ranges by utilizing terahertz frequencies. Beam training at the symbol rate's high frequency in wireless connections helps mitigate this short range but demands substantial power consumption. In rateless codeword beam training protocols, candidate beams are tested sequentially until a strong connection is found, however, this approach isn't optimal due to the codebook's large size at THz frequencies. A method is needed to thin out the codebook while finding efficient beams quickly. This method can be accomplished by teaching a reinforcement learning agent to select the most effective beams from various parts of the codebook for both sender and receiver, based on a small amount of sample data. With access to the entire codebook and no prior knowledge of the channel, the learning agent builds a selection strategy that considers multiple hop constraints, enabling it to retrieve the best beams efficiently.

The interstellar medium's impact on radio signals has been extensively studied, 
offering insights into the large-scale structure of our galaxy. Recently, 
researchers have also begun examining how plasma interactions affect radio 
waves in smaller scales, which could significantly alter how we observe 
pulsars and other powerful electromagnetic sources. In this work, we combine 
existing data sets to create high-resolution maps of the interstellar 
environment along the line of sight to Lighthouse Region, where pulsar B1133+16 
is located. Comparing our findings with observations of the bright, dense region, 
we discover several notable discrepancies. These include an extended, bright 
feature approximately 100 parsecs long, which does not match the expected shape 
based on our galaxy's overall structure. Additionally, we see an unusual 
fluctuation towards the edge of the Milky Way, which our general model fails to 
predict accurately. These discoveries highlight areas where our current 
understanding of our galaxy is incomplete, which could have significant 
implications for future research utilizing radio sources as backlights for 
studying the interstellar medium.

This paper presents a novel generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet, which is designed to capture the quasi-periodic nature of speech and music signals. Building on WaveNet's success in audio signal generation, our model addresses the inefficiency of the original WaveNet in handling periodic patterns due to its use of dilated convolution. By analyzing the characteristics of speech and music sounds, we identified the importance of modeling quasi-periodicity and developed an adaptation in dilated convolution that considers pitch. This developed layer enables the network to effectively capture periodic patterns, but also poses an issue of irreversibility in the generation process. To overcome this limitation, our network incorporates an asymmetric structure in the dilation pattern, thus enabling effective decoding in a quasi-periodic manner. By leveraging the unrolled formulation of the network operation, we derive an equivalence between our model and traditional FIR neural network layers. This equivalence provides the necessary mathematical foundation to effectively train our Quasi-Periodic WaveNet model. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our proposed model over competing models in various speech and music generation tasks, particularly in terms of perceptual quality.

This study introduces MADARi, a web application designed to facilitate the annotation of Advanced Arabic Morphological Analysis and Reconstruction details. Additionally, it can be used for creating custom tagsets, enabling the simultaneous addition of analysis tags to Arabic words. For reference, the web application has been demonstrated with the Bashar corpus, although its capabilities are not limited to this specific corpus.

Researchers have utilized spectral analysis of transiting and transit-transiting exoplanets to investigate their atmospheric compositions, noting successful applications in hot Jupiter studies but a lack of data on temperate and hydrospheric exoplanets. A simple photochemical model was developed to predict the atmospheric chemistries and spectra of these planets, primarily focusing on Mercury-like worlds and temperate Earth analogs. The model highlights significant differences in atmospheric compositions among different types of planets, while also predicting similar spectra in certain cases. Notably, the presence of photodissociated H$_2$ and CH$_4$ absorption features was identified as a potential means to distinguish between different types of atmospheres. Although current spectroscopic capabilities may be similar for Mercury-like Venus and Mercury worlds, next-generation missions are expected to be able to differentiate between these atmospheres and even detect Earth's O$_2$ band from certain types of transits.

To differentiate between a Majorana zero mode and a pseudo-zero-energy peak in a ferromagnetic nanowire system, we suggest utilizing tunneling spectroscopy with an ohmically damped tunnel barrier, achieved through a vacuum gap formed between a ferromagnetic wire and an electrode with frequency-dependent impedance. Numerical simulations of the system show that incorporating an ohmic resistance alters the features of the tunneling spectrum near zero energy, potentially enabling the distinction between a true Majorana zero-mode and a pseudo-peak.

The development of advanced vision systems that operate reliably in unfavorable conditions and identify multiple objects simultaneously has significantly accelerated in recent years. These systems can now detect and classify various road problems, such as cracks, potholes, and signage issues, from captured images. This project aims to develop a comprehensive vision system that can recognize all these defects simultaneously, even in challenging weather conditions. To achieve this goal, the team created an intelligent platform called RoadAtlas, named after the ancient cartography road atlas. This platform includes front-end and back-end components built with RESTful architecture using Django and Django REST framework, providing users with a range of features including data management, image annotation tools, custom algorithm deployment, and performance evaluation through metrics and visualizations. To ensure seamless operation, the team utilized Azure Machine Learning for model training and deployment, along with Azure services for storage, visualization, and real-time data processing.

This study offers a reversible categorical framework for analyzing shadows, which are referred to as 'Bicategorical Xnets' - a new concept without prior usage in a categorical context. We demonstrate that shadows constitute a top-dimensional subcategory within this framework and introduce an integrality constraint on the objects used. Furthermore, the study reveals that the category of shadows is equivalent to the integral segment of the 1-categorical bicategory of Xnets.

This study aims to localize sound sources in an anthropometric room using
probabilistic program synthesis. Unlike typical approach that uses deep
learning in the context of audio source localization, our research takes a
challenging view. We've utilized Hypert and Sleigh to create a rigorous and
R-based data analysis tool. Our tool reads mono audio data, converts it to a
set of 2D time-variant localization options, and outputs a set of 2D coordinates.
We've utilized the created program as an example for verifying and modifying
auditory source localization algorithms, and it can be used to guide the
development of more complex algorithms.

We present a new type of graph neural network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Networks (LGNN), which is based on a relativistic version of a point cloud neural network. LGNN leverages the inherent positive-definite structure of graphs by transforming them into high-dimensional Minkowski spaces, allowing it to effectively capture and process complex relationships between data points. This approach enables LGNN to outperform traditional neural networks that ignore the geometric properties of graphs, and also competes favorably with state-of-the-art GNN methods on various tasks such as node classification, graph classification and node attribute prediction, using both public and private datasets.

The mathematical model that structural acoustic interactions satisfy is structural. This model is equitable because it considers the energy of the involved system. For this system, the formal supply chain represents the rate of change of the system's energy plus the involved system's dissipative terms. Our main achievement is the validation of structural adequacy for the rearrangement identity of the involved system and its surrounding fluid medium, and the proof that the system's energy converges to zero. These conclusions are validated for the case where the involved system and its surrounding fluid medium exhibit damping.

In a new type of tripartite system, we've discovered a way to create a specific coherent state in an optical cavity by transferring the state from mechanical resonators. Our method involves connecting the components in a three-optima arrangement and making steady-state hybrid connections. We've demonstrated that the quality of the transferred state can be controlled through the system's parameters and the transfer process is robust against changes in those parameters. The advantage of using two optical couplers to connect the components lies in the existence of a stable state where the system transfers the specific coherent state, regardless of the exact values of the optical and mechanical parameters. Furthermore, the quality of the transfer can be enhanced to near-perfection by employing suitable settings for the mechanical resonators, a scenario that can be achieved with current available technology.

We examine an expansion of modal $\mu$-calculus that incorporates a choice operator and calculates the equivalence of formulas through binary relations. This analysis enables determination of the modality of a given formula and identifies its underlying structure as a directed graph. Furthermore, this concept can be applied to verify properties in systems modeled with a transition model known as a labeled transition system.

Research on how people value future rewards has largely focused on exponential delay discounting (EDD) rate $r$, which varies between individuals but offers a simple, yet effective, comparative metric. Unfortunately, the traditional EDD framework fails to account for the significantly higher valuation people place on nearer future rewards in exchange for greater risk. We present a revised $r$ scale based on the efficient EDD (e-EDD) theory, which provides a more accurate efficiency-based blood-relative entropy maximization theory to rationally explain decision-making under uncertainty. The revised scale positions the e-EDD parameter $\lambda$ as the fundamental variable driving the market's time preference, where the $\lambda$ scale directly reflects the supply and demand for well-being in the market. Under the e-EDD framework, the central role of the Lagrange multiplier enables a more in-depth understanding of market dynamics influencing the valuation of future well-being and the interplay between supply, demand, risk and time within the market.

In Substantial Gravity's Newtonian limit, multiple harmonic gauges similar to General Relativity's appear. To clarify this, the author examines one such gauge in detail, showing how it yields the standard Newtonian potential and may offer more insights. This task requires examining inhomogeneous metric perturbations and their connection to standard harmonic coordinates, which is explored through a specific example. This exploration may be relevant to research on gravitational waves and the Hubble constant discrepancy.

We investigate signed graphs, which are graphs that have been assigned edges with specific orientations. Recent research on the asymptotic theory of signed graphs has led to a new set of structures called Extended Double Covers (EDCs). EDCs are constructed by combining two other graph structures along with their corresponding edge sets. It is shown through a new theorem that large density signed graphs can be approximated by EDCs; this approximation involves specific parameters and can help in studying properties of homomorphism limits of signed graphs. A specific subclass of edds, consisting of two edge-density graphs with directed edges, is explored to understand its role in determining minimum saturation properties of directed edges.

The Weyy-Wigner function is an effective tool for analyzing the long-term behavior of quantum systems in a Weyl-m phase space. This paper proves that for any quantum system with canonical thermal equilibrium, its Weyl-Wigner representation remains stable over time and accurately reflects the system's interaction with its surroundings. This result holds for systems that follow the Weyl-Wigner product rule. The proof of this theorem is provided for both finite and continuous spectral ranges. Furthermore, the theorem's implications are explored, demonstrating how it can be used to identify steady-state systems and establish the Weyl-Wigner thermal equilibrium state.

The notion of negative absolute temperature has been subject to extensive discussion, often accompanied by skepticism. While some systems, comprising bosons, can attain such temperatures, it's important to note that they represent the exception and must meet specific criteria. It is possible to create two populations of particles, potentially including fermions and bosons, that share the same container and, under certain conditions, negative temperature. In these scenarios, the high temperature limit approaches a state where the two populations reach equilibrium and the chemical potential becomes prominent.

Let G be a finite group of order n, and let A be a subset of G with cardinality m, where n and m are relatively prime integers. If the constrained signed sumset A^+ contains all elements of G, and |A| is sufficiently large in relation to n, then A must be a subset that almost covers G. This paper proves an equalities version of the constrained sumset problem and obtains narrowings of the equalities narrowing by using the representation theorem of group algebra.

Historical evidence and statistical data highlight the crucial role of colorectal cancer screening in saving lives, emphasizing the need for accurate and timely detection and classification of polyps from histological images to guide further treatment procedures.

Deep learning applications are becoming increasingly common in the field of polyp analysis, yet working with such images poses technical challenges due to the sensitive nature of the images and the potential risk of revealing information about the individuals depicted.

To facilitate research and development of effective polyp analysis methods, we have created the UniToPatho dataset, a comprehensive collection of annotated colorectal images that span a wide range of polyp types.

Consisting of nearly 8000 annotated images, the dataset includes numerous examples of various types of polyps, providing researchers with a valuable resource for evaluating and improving detection, segmentation, and classification techniques using such images.

A novel numerical method has been developed to address wave propagation and scattering phenomena governed by the time-harmonic Schrödinger equation, utilizing absorbing layers that gradually increase in thickness with frequency. This method ensures that numerical simulations remain accurate by ensuring the numerical wavelength is always at least as long as a specific constant multiplied by the physical wavelength. Compared to traditional methods such as perfectly matched layers, this approach does not necessitate truncation errors to diminish exponentially and instead is capable of accurately capturing low-frequency behaviors without being significantly impacted by the highest frequency present.

New constraints on the water content of early planetary building blocks have been established through the water/oxidant balance in the Chelyabinsk and Benenitra meteorites, which are now recognized as extremely dry objects of the outer asteroid belt. These two meteorites, discovered in 2009 and 2011 respectively, exhibited a unique set of features, including high levels of reduction, in their olivine crystals that could not be attributed to contamination. The high levels of reduction in these meteorites imply a low water content in the parent asteroids, which in turn suggest that the inner Solar System building blocks were dry and formed in the asteroid belt's inner region as large, dry objects. The findings of the water/oxidant balance in these meteorites now provide crucial evidence for the moist accretion theory of the inner Solar System building blocks. The theory proposes that the process of accretion was alternating between periods of dry and wet accretion, ultimately forming the mixed, water-rich inner Solar System building blocks.

Using the thermodynamic limit of the TQ-equation, we calculate the ground-state energy and quasi-momentum for a specific type of spin chain. This chain consists of N sites and uses an affine quantum-algebra as its local symmetry, which is generated by a set of currents that correspond to the roots of a Lie-algebra. For an important class of these models related to an affine quantum-ZXXZ chain, we derive closed expressions for the eigenvalues of these currents, which are valid within a broad range of model parameters. This allows us to determine the total charges and quasi-momenta for the ground states in the long-spin case, which consists of a single high-spin and multiple short spins. Our work also establishes the affine quantum-algebra symmetry for the affine quantum-ZXXZ Hamiltonians and provides a foundation for applying diagonalisation techniques to study the long-spin spin chains.

Voice translation technology enables the translation of audio content into another language, although existing systems are limited to a finite number of language pairs. In this research, we introduce a novel approach for zero-shot voice translation, allowing for the translation of audio into new, unseen languages. Our method leverages a large language model, specifically LLaMA-7B, to generate high-quality translations while preserving the intended tone and style. We enhance the model's capability for zero-shot task execution by fine-tuning it with a high-quality, manually curated dataset consisting of 1,842 bilingual (Chinese-English) speech translation samples. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our system successfully outperforms existing baseline systems, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach for zero-shot speech translation. Furthermore, our method is accessible through an open-source platform at this link: https://huggingface.co/trainor/llama-vv.

We examine the connection between a central object and multiple peripheral objects in a two-step process. First, we represent the scattering influence of the central object on the peripheral objects using a well-known approach called the method of multipolar decomposition (MoMD). This method breaks down the scattering into distinct components, known as multipoles, based on their order. Next, we investigate how the peripheral objects interact with each other through the mediating effect of the central object, classifying this interaction by its multipolar order. This method is straightforward to apply and provides a clear visual understanding, but is limited to situations where the peripheral and central objects are separated by a significant distance, typical of optical scenarios.

This study introduces two innovative concepts: the double Young-Capelli bitableau character and the Schur altered symmetric function. We demonstrate that the double Young-Capelli bitableau character relates to the irreducible Schur character through the Schur function altered by the Schur function's alternating product. Additionally, this characterization provides a straightforward derivation of the fermionic Schur function.

Within the most minimal scoto-seesaw model, we examine the consistency between neutrino mass, dark matter credibility, and the stability of the Standard Model vacuum at energy scales beyond 10 TeV. We find a precise correlation between the properties of dark matter and the extent of the Standard Model vacuum's stability, realized through the interplay of two key parameters in this model: the magnitude of the neutrino and the mass of the dark matter, centered around a specific energy scale of approximately 10 TeV. Notably, the minimum and maximum values of the $\nu$-$\chi$ mass range widely, spanning from a few TeV to $10^5$ TeV, predominantly dictated by the magnitude of another key parameter, $a$, which governs the interaction between dark matter and the Standard Model, remaining independent of neutrino and dark matter masses. Furthermore, we investigate the consistency of dark matter with the precision measurements of the electroweak sector and the high-energy tail of the diphoton resonance distribution, noting that certain $\nu$-$\chi$ parameter combinations aligned with minimum vacuum stability criteria may be excluded by dark matter observations, however, this is not the case for all combinations within the $a$ scale of several thousand to hundred thousand TeV.

The concept of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ orbital hybridization is vital for transition metal compounds, yet it has been limitedly studied in 4d and 5d systems. Through experimental and theoretical analysis of LaMnO$_3$, LaRuO$_3$, and LaIrO$_3$, we demonstrate significant $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ orbital mixing in 4d and 5d systems. This finding contradicts the usual assumption of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ orbital separation and shows that multi-orbital interactions must be considered when studying these compounds.

Radiology, as a diagnostic imaging branch, relies heavily on expert knowledge and human judgment.  To overcome staff shortages, radiology institutions are increasingly using AI tools for disease detection and tumor marking.  Current AI methods, based on hand-crafted features and rule-based systems, are difficult to scale and adaptable.  Deep learning-based tumor detection and segmentation, though widely studied, predominantly focus on classification and segmentation accuracy, neglecting the detection of anatomical and physiological feasibility.  This research proposes a new, flexible deep learning approach, incorporating a task-specific,可微分的解剖 structure prior network, for accurate and feasible chest X-ray disease segmentation.  Initially applied to segmenting pulmonary lesions in laterally radiographs, this method demonstrates promising results with an average Dice score of 0.74.  Furthermore, our approach shows greater stiffness in terms of generalization across different datasets and orientation adaptations when compared to leading segmentation methods.  This research is open-source, with code available at https://github.com/yxwang2/CIAS.

Current visualization and examination tools fall short when it comes to
high-dimensionality, interdependent variables commonly found in real-world
scenarios. To address this issue, we've developed an innovative approach that
integrates a novel non-linear technique, known as Vision Elements for Dimensional
Analysis (ViDa), with traditional examination methods. Our approach allows us to
create clear, easy-to-understand graphical representations by combining common
examination methods with the unique ViDa method. We've implemented this
approach in a web-based tool called ViDaExpert, which can be accessed for free
and utilized to create impressive graphical representations. We've demonstrated
the effectiveness of our approach by examining real-world datasets, including
real estate prices and restaurant reviews.

This paper provides a speeded-up computation of Newtonian potentials on a two-dimensional flat area using the finite element method. Our algorithm utilizes standard, unstructured triangular elements and is particularly efficient for large-scale computations, as it avoids the slow calculation of Gaussian integrals by leveraging a simplified matrix operation. We have compared our method to the traditional approach and conducted a timing analysis, which shows significant time savings, which we've broken down into various computational steps.
